findings.passage: “A statewide mandate to lock up your handguns is unenforceable,” Olson said. “Under this language even off-duty law enforcement officers, who are never really off duty, would have to lock up their weapons after their shift had ended.”
findings.note: From his official House release after the House passed three gun bills (lost/stolen reporting deadline, trigger activator definition, locked storage). He says the storage mandate cannot be enforced.

findings.passage: “It would be one thing if the majority was approving measures that would hold criminals accountable and put an end to violent crime,” Olson said. “But in this case, it is targeting law abiding citizens and in one case, actually turning a gun owner into a criminal.”
findings.note: From his official House release. He says the three bills target law-abiding gun owners, and says one would make a gun owner a criminal. The release also says he voted against all three and describes the 2023 universal background checks and red flag orders as laws the majority and the governor enacted.

findings.passage: Also included is language relating to scope of practice and a binary trigger ban for firearms. Olson said no one had a chance to review this massive proposal prior to a vote being taken.
findings.note: Session-end release issued in his name. It notes that a binary trigger ban was in the 1,430-page omnibus bill passed at the end of session, and he objects that no one could review it before the vote. The release also lists new laws that 'punish law-abiding gun owners' among his criticisms.

findings.passage: I also had the opportunity to visit Federal Ammunition in Anoka this week a long standing Minnesota manufacturer that employs over 1,400 people and plays a vital role in both our economy and our nation’s defense industry.
findings.note: From his legislative update newsletter. He visited an ammunition maker and links the visit to supporting local manufacturing and protecting Second Amendment rights (the sentence after this one).
